[PRIOR RECORD (advice_review; decision_status: tl_rejected; execution_status: not_executed; outcome_status: resolved_in_checked_tasks) - history, not a standing rule.]
## Evidence available at review

The September 7 support notes cover RP14-Z011 and RP14-Z012 on a training workstation. At 200% browser zoom, the bottom of the form, including Submit, lay below the visible area. The button was not observed to be disabled. Returning the browser to 100% exposed the button, and both tasks produced a submission receipt: SIM-SUB-RP14-Z011 and SIM-SUB-RP14-Z012.

No network error or server rejection was recorded. These two cases were already resolved before this advice review; no action in response to the rejected recommendation has been executed.

## Prior ThreadSense advice

Add a standard FAQ answer telling every tutor with a Submit problem to reset browser zoom to 100% before reporting the issue.

# RP-20260916-01 — Approve tie calibration advice

## Context
The prior batch's calibration packet contained one pair differing only in wording and another in which one response omitted a fact needed for the user's request. Reviewers were using “slightly clearer” without explaining whether it changed usefulness.

## Suggested advice
The simulated Advisor proposed a brief alignment announcement and a review of eight sampled pairs, using the existing meaningful-quality-difference criterion.

## TL approval
Alex approved the proposal. Ask reviewers to identify the actual user-facing benefit; a cosmetic wording preference alone is not sufficient. Keep material accuracy or instruction defects visible rather than forcing ties.

This is a calibration of the existing criterion, not a new numerical preference threshold. The approval covers the batch-14 exercise.

## State
Posting and the review exercise are authorized but not recorded as completed in this approval.
